```{r}

df <- people_counter_processed
# Ensure Date is Date type
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)

#selecting all relevant columns and renaming TotalCount to PedestrianCount. PedestrainCount takes average of CombinedCount 
df_processed<- df%>%
  select(1,3:12, 14:21)%>%
  rename(PedestrianCount = TotalCount)
```

```{ Diagnostic Analysis r}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 1: Diagnostic plot of imbalance_ratio distribution, per counter
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Goal: see whether there's a natural break in the distribution (e.g. most
# days cluster well below 0.95, with a distinct tail near 1.0) rather than
# picking a round number blind. A visible valley in the density is a much
# stronger justification for a cutoff than "it seemed reasonable."

imbalance_diagnostic <- df_processed %>%
  mutate(
    imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1),
    CombinedCount = CombinedCount
  ) %>%
  filter(!CounterID == "Tidepool Lot 2")

# Overall distribution, all counters pooled
ggplot(imbalance_diagnostic, aes(x = imbalance_ratio)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99), linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of directional imbalance ratio",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines mark candidate thresholds (0.85 / 0.90 / 0.95 / 0.99)",
    x = "imbalance_ratio = max(In, Out) / CombinedCount",
    y = "Count of days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Per-counter, since a "natural" imbalance (e.g. a one-directional loop
# entrance) at one site could mimic malfunction at another
ggplot(imbalance_diagnostic, aes(x = imbalance_ratio)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99), linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of directional imbalance ratio by counter",
    x = "imbalance_ratio", y = "Count of days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Ratio vs. volume, since a mismatch on a high-volume day is more likely a
# genuine signal than the same ratio on a near-zero-count day
ggplot(imbalance_diagnostic, aes(x = CombinedCount, y = imbalance_ratio)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.90, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title = "Imbalance ratio vs. daily combined count",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines mark the current cutoff (ratio > 0.90, count > 50)",
    x = "CombinedCount", y = "imbalance_ratio"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# If you have known hardware-outage dates (e.g. the Tidepool Lot 1 outage
# you already handled), overlay them here to check whether your threshold
# actually catches known-bad periods without over-flagging normal days:
#
known_outage_dates <- as.Date(c("2026-03-15", "2026-03-26", "2026-02-27", "2026-02-27", "2026-03-08", "2026-03-12", "2026-03-16", "2026-03-26", "2026-03-21"))

imbalance_diagnostic %>%
  mutate(known_outage = Date %in% known_outage_dates) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = imbalance_ratio, fill = known_outage)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 2: Threshold sensitivity analysis
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Goal: instead of defending one arbitrary (ratio, min_volume) pair, show
# that downstream conclusions are stable across a reasonable range. Vary
# both parameters together, since they jointly determine what gets flagged.

clean_with_threshold <- function(df, ratio_thresh, min_volume) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1),
      is_mismatch = imbalance_ratio > ratio_thresh & CombinedCount > min_volume,
      PedestriansIn_clean = if_else(is_mismatch, NA_real_, PedestriansIn),
      PedestriansOut_clean = if_else(is_mismatch, NA_real_, PedestriansOut)
    ) %>%
    filter(!CounterID == "Tidepool Lot 2")
}

# Grid of candidate thresholds to test
threshold_grid <- expand_grid(
  ratio_thresh = c(0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99),
  min_volume = c(25, 50, 75)
)

# --- Diagnostic-level summary: how much data gets flagged at each setting ---
flag_summary <- threshold_grid %>%
  mutate(
    result = map2(ratio_thresh, min_volume, function(rt, mv) {
      cleaned <- clean_with_threshold(df_processed, rt, mv)
      cleaned %>%
        summarise(
          n_days = n(),
          n_flagged = sum(is_mismatch, na.rm = TRUE),
          pct_flagged = round(100 * n_flagged / n_days, 2)
        )
    })
  ) %>%
  unnest(result)

print(flag_summary)

ggplot(flag_summary, aes(x = ratio_thresh, y = pct_flagged, color = factor(min_volume))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Share of days flagged as mismatched, across threshold settings",
    x = "Ratio threshold", y = "% of days flagged",
    color = "Min. volume floor"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# --- Downstream-conclusion-level check ---
# Swap in whatever your actual downstream summary is (annual totals from
# your STL/ETS forecast, Kruskal-Wallis test statistic, etc.). Below is a
# simple stand-in using mean daily count by counter as the outcome to track;
# replace `downstream_summary()` with your real pipeline so you're testing
# stability of the number you actually report, not a proxy for it.

downstream_summary <- function(df_processed) {
  df_processed %>%
    group_by(CounterID) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_daily_count_clean = mean(CombinedCount[!is_mismatch], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

sensitivity_results <- threshold_grid %>%
  mutate(
    result = map2(ratio_thresh, min_volume, function(rt, mv) {
      clean_with_threshold(df_processed, rt, mv) %>% downstream_summary()
    })
  ) %>%
  unnest(result)

# Plot how the reported summary statistic moves as thresholds change.
# A roughly flat set of lines per counter = your conclusions are robust to
# the exact cutoff, which is the strongest defense of an otherwise arbitrary
# choice. Sharp jumps = the threshold IS doing meaningful work, and you should
# pick + justify it more carefully (or report a range instead of a point estimate).
ggplot(sensitivity_results, aes(x = ratio_thresh, y = mean_daily_count_clean, color = factor(min_volume))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Downstream summary statistic across threshold settings",
    subtitle = "Flat lines = conclusions robust to threshold choice",
    x = "Ratio threshold", y = "Mean daily count (cleaned)",
    color = "Min. volume floor"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# NOTE: free_y scaling above zooms each panel to its own tiny range, which
# can make small absolute jumps look dramatic (or flat ones look flatter
# than they are). Check % change, not just visual slope, before calling a
# line "robust." Also, mean_daily_count_clean is mechanically biased to
# rise as ratio_thresh loosens, since loosening the threshold un-excludes
# high-volume flagged days back into the average. That confound alone can
# produce an upward-sloping line even with no real malfunction signal.
 
# --- Comparison plot: does the downstream statistic move only where a real
# cluster of days gets un-flagged, or does it drift independent of that? ---
# If a jump in the summary statistic lines up with a jump in pct_flagged,
# that's good evidence the jump is being driven by a real cluster of
# borderline days rather than by the mechanical confound above. If the
# summary keeps drifting even where pct_flagged is flat, that's a sign
# something else (e.g. seasonality, a handful of high-volume outlier days
# unrelated to mismatch) is driving it, not the threshold choice itself.
 
comparison_data <- flag_summary %>%
  select(ratio_thresh, min_volume, pct_flagged) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  left_join(
    sensitivity_results %>% select(CounterID, ratio_thresh, min_volume, mean_daily_count_clean),
    by = c("ratio_thresh", "min_volume")
  ) %>%
  # scale both series to 0-1 within each counter so they're comparable on
  # one axis regardless of their native units
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_flagged_scaled = (pct_flagged - min(pct_flagged)) / (max(pct_flagged) - min(pct_flagged)),
    mean_count_scaled = (mean_daily_count_clean - min(mean_daily_count_clean)) /
      (max(mean_daily_count_clean) - min(mean_daily_count_clean))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pct_flagged_scaled, mean_count_scaled),
    names_to = "series", values_to = "scaled_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(series = recode(series,
    pct_flagged_scaled = "% days flagged",
    mean_count_scaled = "Mean daily count (cleaned)"
  ))
 
ggplot(comparison_data, aes(x = ratio_thresh, y = scaled_value, color = series, linetype = factor(min_volume))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID) +
  labs(
    title = "Percent of days flagged vs. downstream summary statistic",
    subtitle = "Both series rescaled 0-1 per counter for comparability. Jumps that line up = real signal; jumps that don't = check for a confound.",
    x = "Ratio threshold", y = "Scaled value (0-1 within counter)",
    color = "Series", linetype = "Min. volume floor"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# NOTE ON THE ABOVE: in practice both series move together at EVERY
# threshold value, not just at a few jump points, because loosening the
# ratio threshold mechanically un-excludes high-volume days from the mean
# at every step. That makes "do the lines jump together" uninformative as
# a check, since they're always co-moving by construction. What IS useful
# from that plot is the *shape* of the cyan line alone: Lighthouse and
# Bayside Trail plateau (rise, then flatten), meaning there's a bounded
# cluster of high-count days getting excluded and then nothing more above
# that ratio. Oceanside Trail 1 and Tidepool Lot 1 never plateau, meaning
# there's no ratio value where the result settles, so mean-count alone
# can't identify a "correct" threshold for those two.
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 3: Direct check - are flagged days actually anomalous?
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sidesteps the mean-count confound above entirely, by comparing the raw
# CombinedCount distribution of flagged vs. unflagged days directly, rather
# than looking at a downstream statistic that's mechanically tied to the
# flag. If flagged days sit distinctly higher (or lower) than the bulk of
# unflagged days, that's real evidence they're anomalous. If the two
# distributions overlap heavily, the flag isn't distinguishing a genuinely
# different population, it is just cutting an arbitrary slice out of a
# continuum.
 
# Uses your originally stated threshold (ratio > 0.95, CombinedCount > 50).
# Change ratio_thresh / min_volume below to check other candidate cutoffs.
flagged_vs_unflagged <- clean_with_threshold(df_processed, ratio_thresh = 0.95, min_volume = 50)
 
ggplot(flagged_vs_unflagged, aes(x = CombinedCount, fill = is_mismatch)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "CombinedCount distribution: flagged vs. unflagged days",
    subtitle = "Heavy overlap = flag may just be slicing a continuum, not isolating anomalies",
    x = "CombinedCount", y = "Density", fill = "Flagged as mismatch"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
 
# Boxplot version, often easier to read for skewed count data
ggplot(flagged_vs_unflagged, aes(x = is_mismatch, y = CombinedCount, fill = is_mismatch)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "CombinedCount: flagged vs. unflagged days",
    x = "Flagged as mismatch", y = "CombinedCount"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
 
# Formal check: Wilcoxon rank-sum test per counter, since CombinedCount is
# typically right-skewed (matches the non-parametric approach you're
# already using elsewhere, e.g. Kruskal-Wallis / Dunn's)
flagged_vs_unflagged %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_flagged = sum(is_mismatch, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unflagged = sum(!is_mismatch, na.rm = TRUE),
    wilcox_p = tryCatch(
      wilcox.test(CombinedCount ~ is_mismatch)$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 4: Binomial-test-based flagging (replaces ratio + volume floor)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Instead of a fixed ratio threshold plus an arbitrary volume floor, test
# each day directly: is the observed in/out split significantly different
# from the counter's expected split, given how many total crossings there
# were that day? This absorbs the floor's job (protect low-count days from
# noise) into the math automatically, since the confidence interval on a
# proportion is wide when n is small and narrow when n is large. The only
# real choice left is the significance level (alpha), which is a more
# standard and defensible knob than a chosen ratio value.
#
# IMPORTANT: this assumes an expected split per counter. Don't assume 50/50
# blindly, since a counter on a loop trail or near a lot with directional
# flow bias may have a genuinely uneven normal split. Estimate it from the
# bulk of the data (e.g. median split, excluding known-bad periods) rather
# than assuming symmetry.
 
# Step 1: estimate each counter's expected split from its own historical
# data. Uses the median daily proportion as a robust estimate of "normal,"
# since a straight overall mean could be pulled by the very malfunctioning
# days you're trying to detect.
expected_splits <- df_processed %>%
  filter(!CounterID == "Tidepool Lot 2", CombinedCount > 0) %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  summarise(
    expected_prop_in = median(PedestriansIn / CombinedCount, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
 
print(expected_splits)
# Check these before proceeding: a value near 0.5 suggests a balanced
# in/out trail; anything notably off 0.5 means that counter has a genuine
# directional bias and the binomial test below correctly accounts for it,
# whereas the old ratio+floor rule would not have.
 
# Step 2: run a per-day binomial test against each counter's own expected
# split. This is row-wise, so it can be slow on very large datasets -
# consider using purrr::pmap or vectorizing with binom.confint from the
# `binom` package if this becomes a bottleneck.
binom_flagged <- df_processed %>%
  filter(!CounterID == "Tidepool Lot 2") %>%
  left_join(expected_splits, by = "CounterID") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    binom_p = if_else(
      CombinedCount > 0,
      tryCatch(
        binom.test(PedestriansIn, CombinedCount, p = expected_prop_in)$p.value,
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      ),
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # PRACTICAL significance, alongside statistical significance: at large
    # CombinedCount, even a trivial 52/48 deviation from the expected split
    # will hit p < 0.01, because binomial test power scales with n. That's
    # correct math but not a useful malfunction flag. Cohen's h is a
    # scale-free effect size for comparing two proportions (does not
    # inflate with n the way the p-value does), letting us require the
    # deviation to actually be LARGE, not just statistically detectable.
    observed_prop_in = PedestriansIn / CombinedCount,
    cohens_h = 2 * asin(sqrt(observed_prop_in)) - 2 * asin(sqrt(expected_prop_in)),
    # min_effect: tune this. 0.5 is a conventional "medium" effect size
    # threshold for Cohen's h; raise it (e.g. 0.8, "large") to be stricter
    # about what counts as a real malfunction rather than routine variation.
    is_mismatch_binom = !is.na(binom_p) & binom_p < 0.01 & abs(cohens_h) > 0.5,
    PedestriansIn_clean_binom = if_else(is_mismatch_binom, NA_real_, PedestriansIn),
    PedestriansOut_clean_binom = if_else(is_mismatch_binom, NA_real_, PedestriansOut)
  )
 
# Step 3: compare the binomial rule against your original ratio + floor rule
comparison_rules <- binom_flagged %>%
  mutate(
    imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1),
    is_mismatch_ratio = imbalance_ratio > 0.95 & CombinedCount > 50
  ) %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_days = n(),
    n_flagged_ratio = sum(is_mismatch_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flagged_binom = sum(is_mismatch_binom, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flagged_both = sum(is_mismatch_ratio & is_mismatch_binom, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flagged_ratio_only = sum(is_mismatch_ratio & !is_mismatch_binom, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flagged_binom_only = sum(!is_mismatch_ratio & is_mismatch_binom, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
 
print(comparison_rules)
# n_flagged_ratio_only: days the old rule caught that the binomial test
# says are NOT statistically anomalous, given their volume - candidates for
# false positives under the old rule (likely low-volume noisy days).
# n_flagged_binom_only: days the binomial test catches that the old rule
# missed - candidates for false negatives under the old rule (e.g. a
# high-volume day with a moderate but statistically significant deviation
# that never crossed the 0.95 ratio line).
 
# Visual: which days each rule disagrees on, plotted by volume and ratio,
# to see whether disagreement clusters at low volume (as expected if the
# binomial test is correctly rescuing low-count days from the old floor)
comparison_rules_detail <- binom_flagged %>%
  mutate(
    imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1),
    is_mismatch_ratio = imbalance_ratio > 0.95 & CombinedCount > 50,
    agreement = case_when(
      is_mismatch_ratio & is_mismatch_binom ~ "Both flag",
      is_mismatch_ratio & !is_mismatch_binom ~ "Ratio only",
      !is_mismatch_ratio & is_mismatch_binom ~ "Binomial only",
      TRUE ~ "Neither"
    )
  )
 
ggplot(
  comparison_rules_detail %>% filter(agreement != "Neither"),
  aes(x = CombinedCount, y = imbalance_ratio, color = agreement)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title = "Where the ratio+floor rule and binomial test disagree",
    subtitle = "Points where only one rule flags the day",
    x = "CombinedCount", y = "imbalance_ratio", color = "Flagged by"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
 
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 5: Median/MAD-based robust cutoff on imbalance_ratio, per counter
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mean +/- 2 SD is not appropriate here for two reasons:
#  1. imbalance_ratio is bounded in [0.5, 1] and typically right-skewed
#     (most days balanced, thin tail toward 1.0), not normal, so mean +/- 2SD
#     can land above 1.0 (meaningless) or miss real anomalies.
#  2. SD itself is not robust: the malfunctioning days you're trying to
#     detect are exactly the days that inflate the SD, which then pushes
#     the "2 SD" cutoff further out and makes those same days harder to
#     catch (masking). Median and MAD are robust to this because the
#     median isn't dragged around by extreme values.
#
# This computes both versions per counter so you can see how much they
# disagree; a big gap between them is itself informative about how skewed
# a given counter's distribution is.
 
robust_cutoffs <- df_processed %>%
  filter(!CounterID == "Tidepool Lot 2") %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  summarise(n_zero_volume_days = sum(CombinedCount == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
 
robust_cutoffs <- df_processed %>%
  filter(!CounterID == "Tidepool Lot 2", CombinedCount > 0) %>%
  # CombinedCount > 0 excludes zero-traffic days, not as an arbitrary floor
  # but because imbalance_ratio is undefined/uninformative with no crossings
  # at all (0/1 = 0 by construction). Leaving those in collapses the median
  # and MAD toward zero, which produces a meaningless near-zero cutoff.
  mutate(imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1)) %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_ratio = mean(imbalance_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_ratio = sd(imbalance_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_ratio = median(imbalance_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    mad_ratio = mad(imbalance_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),  # constant = 1.4826 by default, consistent with SD for normal data
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(robust_cutoffs, by = "CounterID") %>%
  mutate(
    cutoff_sd = mean_ratio + 2 * sd_ratio,
    cutoff_mad = median_ratio + 2 * mad_ratio,
    # Flag if either cutoff exceeds the ratio's natural ceiling of 1.0 -
    # a sign that mean+/-2SD isn't a meaningful cutoff for that counter
    cutoff_sd_invalid = cutoff_sd >= 1
  )
 
print(robust_cutoffs)
# Check n_zero_volume_days per counter - if it's a large share of total
# days for any counter, that's worth understanding on its own (seasonal
# closure? known outage period? genuinely near-zero off season traffic?)
# separately from the malfunction-detection question.
 
# Apply both cutoffs per counter and flag days
robust_flagged <- df_processed %>%
  filter(!CounterID == "Tidepool Lot 2") %>%
  mutate(imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1)) %>%
  left_join(robust_cutoffs %>% select(CounterID, cutoff_sd, cutoff_mad), by = "CounterID") %>%
  mutate(
    is_mismatch_sd = imbalance_ratio > cutoff_sd,
    is_mismatch_mad = imbalance_ratio > cutoff_mad
  )
 
# Modified z-score for reference/plotting (0.6745 rescales MAD to be
# comparable to SD under normality, the standard convention)
robust_flagged <- robust_flagged %>%
  left_join(robust_cutoffs %>% select(CounterID, median_ratio, mad_ratio), by = "CounterID") %>%
  mutate(modified_z = 0.6745 * (imbalance_ratio - median_ratio) / mad_ratio)
 
ggplot(robust_flagged, aes(x = imbalance_ratio)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = cutoff_sd), linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = cutoff_mad), linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean+2SD (orange) vs. Median+2MAD (red) cutoffs, per counter",
    subtitle = "Where these diverge a lot, the SD-based cutoff is likely distorted by the outliers it's trying to catch",
    x = "imbalance_ratio", y = "Count of days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
 
# --- Three-way comparison: ratio+floor vs. binomial+effect-size vs. median/MAD ---
three_way_comparison <- binom_flagged %>%
  mutate(imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1)) %>%
  left_join(robust_cutoffs %>% select(CounterID, cutoff_mad), by = "CounterID") %>%
  mutate(
    is_mismatch_ratio = imbalance_ratio > 0.95 & CombinedCount > 50,
    is_mismatch_mad = imbalance_ratio > cutoff_mad
  ) %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_days = n(),
    n_flagged_ratio = sum(is_mismatch_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flagged_binom = sum(is_mismatch_binom, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flagged_mad = sum(is_mismatch_mad, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flagged_all_three = sum(is_mismatch_ratio & is_mismatch_binom & is_mismatch_mad, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
 
print(three_way_comparison)
# n_flagged_all_three, relative to each individual count, is a reasonable
# "high-confidence" core set: days flagged as malfunctioning under three
# methodologically different approaches (an arbitrary-but-stated rule, a
# significance test with an effect-size floor, and a robust distributional
# cutoff). Days flagged by only one method are the ones worth the closest
# manual review before deciding whether to exclude them.
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# Cleaning data looking at how to deal with outliers
# Date Range (07-01-2025 to 06-30-2026) CHANGE FOR ANALYSIS
# =============================================================================

trail_data <- df_processed %>%
  mutate(
    # Ratio of the larger direction to the total - if one direction dominates, ratio approaches 1
    imbalance_ratio = pmax(PedestriansIn, PedestriansOut) / pmax(CombinedCount, 1),  # avoid div/0
    # If imbalance ratio is over 0.9, and combined count is more than 50, it will exclude data
    #we chose this combination of ratio and count from diagnostic analysis above
    is_mismatch = imbalance_ratio > 0.9 & CombinedCount > 50,  # tune threshold + minimum volume
    PedestriansIn_clean = if_else(is_mismatch, NA_real_, PedestriansIn),
    PedestriansOut_clean = if_else(is_mismatch, NA_real_, PedestriansOut)
  )%>%
  filter(!CounterID == 'Tidepool Lot 2')%>%
    filter(Date >= as.Date("2025-07-01") & Date <= as.Date("2026-06-30"))

shutdown_start <- as.Date("2025-10-01")
shutdown_end   <- as.Date("2025-11-12")

trail_data <- trail_data %>%
  mutate(is_shutdown = Date >= shutdown_start & Date <= shutdown_end)

# Analysis dataset: no mismatch days, no shutdown days
trail_open <- trail_data %>%
  filter(!is_mismatch, !is_shutdown)
```

```{r}
# Drop zero-count days (October closure and hardware outages). log(0) is
# undefined, and these days reflect missing data, not an absence of visitors
anova_data <- dayofweek_summary %>%
  filter(DailyVisitors > 0)

# Fit one model per counter. Keep log() inside the formula (not a pre-made
# log column) so emmeans knows the response was logged and can back-transform
dow_models <- anova_data %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~ lm(log(DailyVisitors) ~ DayOfWeek, data = .x)),
    emm   = map(model, ~ emmeans(.x, ~ DayOfWeek))
  )

# --- ANOVA tables ---
anova_results <- dow_models %>%
  mutate(anova_tbl = map(model, ~ tidy(anova(.x)))) %>%
  dplyr::select(CounterID, anova_tbl) %>%
  unnest(anova_tbl)

# --- Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons ---
# type = "response" back-transforms, so each contrast is a RATIO of
# geometric mean daily counts (e.g., Saturday / Monday = 2.1)
tukey_results <- dow_models %>%
  mutate(pairs_tbl = map(emm, ~ as.data.frame(
    summary(pairs(.x, adjust = "tukey"), type = "response")))) %>%
  dplyr::select(CounterID, pairs_tbl) %>%
  unnest(pairs_tbl)
print(tukey_results, n = Inf)

# --- Compact letter display: days sharing a letter do not differ ---
# This is the quickest way to see where Friday groups
cld_results <- dow_models %>%
  mutate(letters_tbl = map(emm, function(e) {
    p <- as.data.frame(pairs(e, adjust = "tukey"))
    pvals <- setNames(p$p.value, gsub(" - ", "-", p$contrast))
    lets <- multcompLetters(pvals)$Letters
    tibble(DayOfWeek = names(lets), group = unname(lets))
  })) %>%
  dplyr::select(CounterID, letters_tbl) %>%
  unnest(letters_tbl)
print(cld_results, n = Inf)

library(knitr)
install.packages("kableExtra")
library(kableExtra)


tukey_results %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons by counter") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

cld_results %>%
  kable(caption = "Compact letter display by counter") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)


# --- Weekend vs weekday ratio with 95% CI (Mon-Fri vs Sat-Sun) ---
# Coefficients follow factor level order: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun
# Change to c(rep(-1/4, 4), 0, 1/2, 1/2) to treat Friday as neither
weekend_ratio <- dow_models %>%
  mutate(ratio_tbl = map(emm, ~ as.data.frame(confint(
    contrast(.x, list("Weekend / Weekday" = c(rep(-1/5, 5), 1/2, 1/2))),
    type = "response")))) %>%
  select(CounterID, ratio_tbl) %>%
  unnest(ratio_tbl)
print(weekend_ratio)

weekend_ratio %>%
  kable(caption = "weekend vs weekday ration with confidence interval") %>%
          kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

# =============================================================================
# Residual diagnostics
# =============================================================================
# augment() with data = .y keeps Date and DayOfWeek alongside the residuals
resid_data <- dow_models %>%
  mutate(aug = map2(model, data, ~ augment(.x, data = .y))) %>%
  select(CounterID, aug) %>%
  unnest(aug)

# 1. Residuals vs fitted: look for an even band with no fanning
resid_vs_fitted <- ggplot(resid_data, aes(x = .fitted, y = .std.resid)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.03, alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Fitted values (log scale)", y = "Standardized residuals",
       title = "Residuals vs. fitted values") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

# 2. Normal Q-Q plot: points should follow the line
resid_qq <- ggplot(resid_data, aes(sample = .std.resid)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Standardized residuals",
       title = "Normal Q-Q plot of residuals") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

# 3. Residual spread by day of week: checks equal variance across days
resid_by_day <- ggplot(resid_data, aes(x = DayOfWeek, y = .std.resid)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Day of week", y = "Standardized residuals",
       title = "Residual spread by day of week") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

resid_vs_fitted
resid_qq
resid_by_day

ggsave("./figures/resid_vs_fitted.png", resid_vs_fitted, width = 9, height = 3, dpi = 600)
ggsave("./figures/resid_qq.png", resid_qq, width = 9, height = 3, dpi = 600)
ggsave("./figures/resid_by_day.png", resid_by_day, width = 9, height = 3.5, dpi = 600)

# Days with large residuals, worth checking against outage records
resid_data %>%
  filter(abs(.std.resid) > 3) %>%
  select(CounterID, Date, DayOfWeek, DailyVisitors, .std.resid) %>%
  arrange(CounterID, .std.resid) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# Fed Holiday Comp
# =============================================================================

fed_holiday<- read_excel("./Data/Raw/OPM_holidays25_26.xlsx")

fed_holiday$Date<- as.Date(fed_holiday$Date)
  
holiday_list <- fed_holiday %>% 
  pull(Holiday) %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  na.omit() %>%
  as.character()

trail_data_and_holiday <- trail_data %>%
  filter(is_mismatch == FALSE) %>%
  group_by(CounterID, Date, DayOfWeek) %>%
  summarise(DailyVisitors = sum(PedestrianCount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(fed_holiday %>% select(Date, Holiday), by = "Date")%>%
  mutate(DayOfWeek = factor(DayOfWeek, 
                             levels = c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday",
                                        "Friday","Saturday","Sunday")))


counter_list <- unique(trail_data_and_holiday$CounterID)

holiday_test <- expand_grid(holiday = holiday_list, CounterID = counter_list) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(holiday, CounterID) {
    
    holiday_rows <- trail_data_and_holiday %>% 
      filter(CounterID == !!CounterID, Holiday == !!holiday)
    if (nrow(holiday_rows) == 0) return(NULL)
    
    baseline <- trail_data_and_holiday %>%
      filter(CounterID == !!CounterID, is.na(Holiday), DailyVisitors > 0)
    if (nrow(baseline) < 3) return(NULL)
    
    holiday_val <- mean(holiday_rows$DailyVisitors)
    test <- t.test(baseline$DailyVisitors, mu = holiday_val)
    se <- sd(baseline$DailyVisitors) / sqrt(nrow(baseline))
    
    tibble(
      holiday = holiday,
      CounterID = CounterID,
      mean_dif = holiday_val - mean(baseline$DailyVisitors),
      se_dif = se,
      pval_sig = test$p.value < 0.05
    )
  })

#ggplot the long ways (vert)

ggplot(data = holiday_test) + 
  geom_col(mapping = aes(y = mean_dif, x = fct_rev(holiday), fill = mean_dif)) + 
  geom_errorbar(mapping = aes(x = fct_rev(holiday), ymin = (mean_dif - se_dif), 
                              ymax = (mean_dif + se_dif), width = 0.3),
                color =  'gray48') + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = cal_palette('bigsur2')[1], 
                        mid = '#E0B0FF', 
                        high = cal_palette('fire')[3],
                        midpoint = 0) +
  geom_text(mapping = aes(x = 12, y = -100, label = 'Fewer visitors'), 
            color = 'black', hjust = 0.95, size = 2.5) + 
  geom_text(mapping = aes(x = 12, y = 100, label = 'More visitors'), 
            color = 'black', hjust = 0, size = 2.5) + 
  geom_text(data = filter(holiday_test, pval_sig == TRUE),
            mapping = aes(x = fct_rev(holiday), y = (mean_dif + se_dif + 100), 
                          label = '*'), color = 'black') +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'black') + 
  coord_flip(xlim = c(1,12)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-1000,1000, by = 500), limits = c(-1300,1300)) +
  ylab('Difference in visitation') + 
  xlab('Holiday') +
  labs(fill = 'Mean Dif')+
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = 'right',
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        text = element_text(color = 'black', size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(color = 'black'),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# ggplot the looooong ways (horiz)

ggplot(data = holiday_test) + 
  geom_col(mapping = aes(x = fct_rev(holiday), y = mean_dif, fill = mean_dif)) + 
  geom_errorbar(mapping = aes(x = fct_rev(holiday), ymin = (mean_dif - se_dif), 
                              ymax = (mean_dif + se_dif), width = 0.3),
                color =  'gray48') + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = cal_palette('bigsur2')[1], 
                        mid = '#E0B0FF', 
                        high = cal_palette('fire')[3],
                        midpoint = 0) +
  geom_text(data = filter(holiday_test, pval_sig == TRUE),
            mapping = aes(x = fct_rev(holiday), y = (mean_dif + se_dif + 100), 
                          label = '*'), color = 'black') +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'black') + 
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1200,1200)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-1000,1000, by = 500)) +
  xlab('Holiday') + 
  ylab('Difference in visitation') +
  facet_wrap(~ CounterID) + 
  theme_bw() +

        axis.text = element_text(color = 'black'),
```

```{r}


fed_holiday<-fed_holiday%>%
  filter(Date >= as.Date("2025-07-01") & Date <= as.Date("2026-06-30"))

# Step 1: build daily totals + calendar coordinates
calendar_data <- trail_data %>%
  filter(is_mismatch == FALSE) %>%
  group_by(CounterID, Date, DayOfWeek) %>%
  summarise(DailyVisitors = sum(PedestrianCount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    Year = year(Date),
    Month = factor(format(Date, "%b"), 
                    levels = c("Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec",
                               "Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun")),
    DayOfMonth = day(Date),
    # true calendar-week position: aligns days into real Mon-Sun weeks
    WeekOfMonth = as.integer(format(Date, "%W")) - 
                  as.integer(format(floor_date(Date, "month"), "%W")) + 1,
    Weekday = factor(DayOfWeek, 
                  levels = c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday",
                             "Friday","Saturday","Sunday"))
  )

# Step 2: flag top 10 busiest days per counter
top_flags <- calendar_data %>%
  group_by(CounterID) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = DailyVisitors, n = 10) %>%
  mutate(is_top10 = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(CounterID, Date, is_top10)

# Step 3: flag holidays
holiday_flags <- fed_holiday %>%
  filter(Holiday %in% holiday_list) %>%
  distinct(Date) %>%
  mutate(is_holiday = TRUE)

calendar_data <- calendar_data %>%
  left_join(top_flags, by = c("CounterID", "Date")) %>%
  left_join(holiday_flags, by = "Date") %>%
  mutate(
    is_top10 = replace_na(is_top10, FALSE),
    is_holiday = replace_na(is_holiday, FALSE),
    is_top10_holiday = is_top10 & is_holiday
  )

# Step 4: build one plot per CounterID, faceted by Month
counter_list <- unique(calendar_data$CounterID)

calendar_plots <- map(counter_list, function(ctr) {
  
  plot_data <- calendar_data %>% filter(CounterID == ctr)
  
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Weekday, y = WeekOfMonth, fill = DailyVisitors)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3, width = 1, height = 1) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(plot_data, is_top10), 
              color = "green", linewidth = 0.8, fill = NA) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(plot_data, is_holiday), 
              color = "blue", linewidth = 0.4, fill = NA, width = 0.5, height = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = DayOfMonth), size = 2, color = "white") +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = cal_palette(name = 'fire', n = 10, type = 'continuous'),
                          labels = scales::comma) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = 1:6) +
    facet_wrap(~ Month, nrow = 3) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Daily\nVisitors",
         title = paste("Daily Visitor Activity —", ctr),
         subtitle = "Blue = federal holiday · Green = top 10 busiest days") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),  
      legend.text = element_text(size = 6), 
      legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
}) %>% set_names(counter_list)

calendar_plots[["Bayside Trail"]]
calendar_plots[["Lighthouse"]]
calendar_plots[["Tidepool Lot 1"]]
calendar_plots[["Oceanside Trail 1"]]

walk2(calendar_plots, names(calendar_plots), function(plot, name) {
  ggsave(filename = paste0("./figures/calendar_", str_replace_all(name, " ", "_"), ".png"),
         plot = plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
})
```
